message:
fix(client): the update notice had no button behind it

0.2.114 fixed the client never asking whether there was a new version. It did not
fix what happens when the answer is yes: shell.html had seven buttons and none of
them was an update, and nothing in the page ever sent {"type":"update"} -- which
client_shell_main.cpp has handled all along. The user got a sentence and no way to
act on it.

This is the same failure the whole round has been chasing -- a decision that exists
with nothing calling it -- and the test written to catch it passed anyway, because
it counted call sites of start_update_check and never looked at the action path. A
source grep cannot see this gap: both halves are present, and what is missing is
only that nothing joins them.

So the new test reads no source. It loads the ui/shell.html that ships into a real
WebView2, posts what the production message builders produce, clicks the rendered
element, and asserts a message comes back out. It writes a screenshot so a person
can see what the user sees. Seventeen cases, positive and negative: no offer before
a check, the offer appearing with its version, the click sending, the button dying
so one press is one updater, coming back after a failed start, 나중에 deferring
without touching sign-in, and the offer being withdrawn on sign-out.

The version travels as a field. A page that had to read it out of a Korean sentence
would break the first time the wording did.

Duplicate starts are refused on the native side as well as the page: the page can
disable its button, but a second message can already be in flight when it does.

0.2.115 is published without this button. Those artifacts stay as they are; the fix
travels in the next release.
